city_center.notes: Dallas and Fort Worth grew from railroads carrying cotton, cattle, and later oil across the Texas Blackland Prairie; the Trinity River threads a leveed floodway between downtown Dallas and the west, and Fort Worth still embraces its Longhorn cattle-trade Western heritage. sources: Dallas railroad / cotton / cattle history (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas); Fort Worth Longhorn cattle trade (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Worth,_Texas); Blackland Prairie (worldlandscapearchitect.com).

cultural_notes: Dallas and Fort Worth both grew as products of railroad lines that carried cotton, cattle, and later oil across North and East Texas -- the metroplex's identity is prairie-commerce and cattle trade, not mountain or desert (source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas)

Fort Worth was established in 1849 as an army outpost on a bluff over the Trinity River and became a center of the Texas Longhorn cattle trade; it still embraces its Western heritage, and the Fort Worth Stockyards keep a working cattle-district identity ('Cowtown') (source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Worth,_Texas)

the region sits on the Texas Blackland Prairie, a dark-soil tallgrass prairie now reduced to less than 1% of its original range -- a conservation-toned landscape story (source: worldlandscapearchitect.com Robert L. Crandall Campus)

the Trinity River runs through a wide leveed floodway between downtown Dallas and the residential west side -- an engineered river landscape rather than a natural greenbelt (source: asla.org Trinity River Corridor Design Guidelines; fwweekly.com Shaping Our Heritage)
